messages:
Anna (Sales): FYI Horus Analytics asked if we can run their in-house model for a 4‑week POC. They want latency ~200ms p50, ~50 rps sustained. Can we validate catalog fit and any enterprise blockers? :eyes:
Mike (Solutions): Need the model artifact or HF repo link + config (vocab, tokenizer, seq len). Also: is their model 15B or 30B? That changes routing and variant suggestions.
Anna (Sales): They shipped a tarball last night. Claiming it's a 15B transformer with custom attention. Also attached a security questionnaire PDF from the customer.
Mike (Solutions): OK. Quick preflight: we run a variant compatibility scan and KV cache stress test. Can you drop the tarball in the shared bucket? I'll kick off scans.
deploy-bot: Started model-compat-scan for model_id=horus-fastllm-v2-15b at 2223456800. Results will be posted here.
Tom (Infra): Heads up — custom attention kernels may not map to our optimized path. If it fails, plan B = run quantized fallback or serve on dedicated nodes with custom runtime.
Julia (InfoSec): On the questionnaire: they require KMS-wrapped keys, VPC peering, and SOC2 attestation. Hosted API can be fine for POC only if data residency and KMS are satisfied. For production they'd need Private or Dedicated with contract addendum.
Anna (Sales): They flagged retention = 30 days and want audit logs. Also single‑tenant isolation preferred.
Mike (Solutions): For latency: if model can't hit 200ms with batching disabled, we can try KV prefix caching + small n_ctx to reduce cost. Suggest creating two variants: fastllm-v2-15b-q4 (8-bit/quant) and fastllm-v2-7b-fallback. We'll A/B route by latency.
Tom (Infra): VM/GPU ask: 2xA100 for the 15B quant variant looks safe for 50 rps with batching. Dedicated pool recommended. If customer wants lower price, we can do shared hosted with scaled down throughput and stricter rate limits.
Mike (Solutions): Rough POC pricing estimate for 1M tokens/month on dedicated pool: $X,000/mo (includes reserved GPU + network). Hosted on-demand would be ~20-30% higher per-token. I'll post numbers once infra confirms.
Anna (Sales): Customer also asked about function calling/structured output compatibility. Are we good?
Mike (Solutions): Should be fine — confirm model supports JSONL/structured outputs. If not, we can wrap postprocessor.
Julia (InfoSec): Checklist to unblock: 1) provide signed SOC2 report or customer acceptance to use Redwood SOC2; 2) confirm KMS provider (AWS KMS ok) + key policy; 3) define retention/audit requirements. Once those are in, I can sign off for a Private trial.
Anna (Sales): I'll send the questionnaire answers and the tarball to the shared bucket by EOD and schedule a call with Horus for Tuesday.
Tom (Infra): I'll reserve a small Dedicated test pool tomorrow and run dry‑runs of the quantized variant.
Mike (Solutions): Plan of record: 1) run compat scan (in progress), 2) build q4 quant variant, 3) KV cache stress test, 4) run latency/throughput benchmarks, 5) share pricing + infra ask.
Anna (Sales): Perfect — tagging next steps: I'll ping Horus that we have a plan and ask them to sign the DPA addendum for the POC. :thumbsup:
Mike (Solutions): If compat-scan flags custom ops, we may need model conversion help from Applied ML. @Julia @Tom I might loop them in depending on results.
deploy-bot: model-compat-scan completed for model_id=horus-fastllm-v2-15b at 2223456890. Summary: tokenizer OK, custom attention layer uses unsupported op 'rotary_custom'; fallback recommended. See attached logs.
Mike (Solutions): rotatory_custom -> likely patchable but needs build. Two options: ask Horus for a HF-compatible variant OR build a wrapper in our runtime (longer). Recommend asking for a HF/PTX export.
Anna (Sales): I'll ask them for a HF export and meanwhile request consent for Dedicated test. Thanks team.
Julia (InfoSec): Keep the security thread linked; don't transmit PII in the bucket. Use encrypted transfer.
Tom (Infra): Noted. I'll start the quant build once we have the artifact.
Anna (Sales): Closing loop for now — will report back after the HF export or call with Horus.
